business_scope.primary_industry_name: Video Game Kernel-Level Anti-Cheat and Integrity Middleware

stage_1.expense_line_item: REQ name declaration (attestation de nom) — pre-incorporation name clearance
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — REQ official fee schedule (CAD 45)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA), sections 10-31 (incorporation), 43-44 (registered office), 102-110 (directors and officers), 214-218 (records)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), operated by the Directeur de l'état civil et du registre des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) submitted electronically via the CliquezAffaires online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under QBCA; shares may be issued for any consideration, including nominal amounts, without statutory escrow provisions
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the corporation adopt its Articles of Incorporation as filed and confirm the appointment of the sole director. That the corporation subscribe for the initial shares as set out in the director's written resolution and allocate such shares to the subscriber named therein. That the registered office be established at the address indicated in the Articles, and the named counsel be authorized to file the initial address declaration. That the following officers be appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until successors are elected. That the banking resolution be adopted, authorizing the signing officers to open accounts and execute all banking documents. That the directors accept all statutory obligations under the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Reservation, and Declaration of Sufficiency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name search via CliquezAffaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed corporation name (e.g., 'Anti-Cheat Integrity Corp.'). Obtain a certificate of name reservation from REQ. If using a number name or a legal name including English-only terms, ensure compliance with Quebec language laws (Charter of the French Language) and apply for necessary permits if the name is considered non-French.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and alternate names
Proof of Canadian or Quebec legal presence for name eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file a revised name request with additional supporting marks, submit a reasoned argument for linguistic compliance, or adopt a number name (e.g., 1234567 Canada Inc.) and register a business style later.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization, and Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) via CliquezAffaires electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of incorporation in the prescribed form, including corporate name, share structure (classes, rights, restrictions), director information, and registered office address. All incorporators must sign electronically or by manual signature; if any director is non-resident of Canada or non-Canadian, no special authorization is needed. Submit the articles via CliquezAffaires and pay the filing fee using credit card, debit, or Interac.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity for each incorporator or director (e.g., photocopy of passport signed by a notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query (e.g., incomplete language, missing consent, or fee error), the filing is returned to the online portal. Correct the affected fields, resubmit without double payment, and the same filing number retains priority. If the query is jurisdictional (e.g., reserved name conflict), file a new name reservation and link it to the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registering Initial Address Declaration and Minutes Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - address declaration filing; internal minutes book manuals governed by QBCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of incorporation, file the initial address declaration (Déclaration initiale d'adresse) with REQ, identifying the registered office, current mailing address, director names, and residency. The address declaration may be filed separately online. Simultaneously, prepare the corporate records book (registre des procès-verbaux) containing the articles, by-laws, minutes of first board meeting, share register, and registered office notice.
required_dossiers: Directors' complete residential addresses and Canadian residency status (if any)
Official corporate email and mailing address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the address declaration is rejected for typographic or address-format errors, correct and resubmit. Late filing penalties may apply if the 15-day deadline is missed; apply for administrative cancellation or reduction of the penalty by providing a reasonable justification under the QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate governance (directors acting under QBCA ss. 97-164), not filed with REQ but recorded in the registered office minutes book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first meeting of the board of directors (can be held by written resolution signed by all directors per QBCA s. 152). Adopt the pro-forma resolution covering share issuance, registered office adoption, officer appointments (President, Secretary, Treasurer), banking resolution, and approval of corporate by-laws. Issue share certificates to the initial subscriber and record all transfers in the share register.
required_dossiers: Notice and agenda of the first board meeting (or waiver of notice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer cannot serve initially, the board may appoint a successor by board resolution; verify that the initial address declaration is updated with the REQ within 10 days of any change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Provincial and Federal Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (for QST, payroll deductions) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the new corporation for a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online or by phone. Elect to collect Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and GST/HST, provide the registered office contact, and select the fiscal year end (e.g., December 31). Also register for employer payroll deduction accounts (source deductions and employer contributions) if hiring employees.
required_dossiers: Director and principal business contact details
Bank account details for GST/HST and QST refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or CRA/Revenu Québec requests full details, complete the missing fields online. Retroactive registration may be granted if the request is made within 30 days of incorporation; otherwise, apply for penalty relief under the Excise Tax Act and QST Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Licensing and Permit Verification for Software Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec Business Registration Portal, and local municipal authorities (e.g., Ville de Montréal) for commercial occupancy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an anti-cheat engine middleware company operating as a software vendor, verify that no industry-specific operational license is required under Quebec law. If offering services to gaming companies, ensure that the business does not engage in regulated gambling activities. Register for the municipal business permit (if maintaining a physical office) and confirm that the office lease allows technology operations. If employing staff, register with the CNESST (occupational health and safety) and the Commission de la construction if applicable—here not applicable for office-based developers.
required_dossiers: Business description and physical location declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipal inspector requires a compliance notice, obtain a certificate of authorization from the local arrondissement or city hall. If CNESST registration is disputed, provide employee classification and payroll records to establish that the business is office/commercial within its scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no manufacturing or physical industrialization of goods; software development and middleware licensing activities are not subject to industrial permits from the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operational license required for anti-cheat engine software; the entity only requires ordinary corporate registration and municipal occupancy permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based software design and development does not constitute a designated project under the Quebec Environmental Quality Act (EQA) and no environmental impact assessment or registration is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Non-applicable; operations generate no industrial wastewater or VOC emissions. If housed in an office building, standard municipal sanitary sewer and building code ventilation standards apply (Québec Construction Code S-24). Workplace electronic waste disposal must follow provincial recycling rules (REPER technology products).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for office premises per the Quebec Fire Safety Code (chapter VIII of the Safety Code) must be obtained from the local municipal fire prevention service. Structural load inspections are not required for standard low-density office occupancy; however, the building lease must meet the Quebec Construction Code for the intended occupancy category. Occupational health and safety registration with the CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) is mandatory if the company has employees, including the establishment of a prevention program. First aid equipment and evacuation signage must be maintained per CNESST standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) - federal tax authority for GST/HST and federal corporate income tax, official portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Revenu Quebec - Quebec provincial tax authority for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec provincial corporate income tax, official portal: revenuquebec.ca/en/; the two agencies coordinate registration and exchange taxpayer information for registrants located in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign- or Canadian-incorporated entity carrying on the gaming anti-cheat middleware business in Quebec obtains its tax identity via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1: (1) apply for a nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) in the name of the Quebec-registered or extra-provincial corporation; (2) add program account RC-1 for GST/HST and, when applicable, RP-1 for payroll and RM-1 for import/export transactions; (3) register separately with Revenu Quebec for the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and QST account, or be auto-registered for QST when the corporation has a permanent establishment in Quebec; (4) provide the certificate of incorporation, by-laws, registered office address in Quebec, director identification, and proof of authorized signatory. No minimum share capital is required and no Canadian residency of shareholders is mandated. Once registered, the BN and QST account allow filing via CRA My Business Account and Revenu Quebec online services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide US-style check-the-box or pass-through elections for business corporations; federal and Quebec corporate tax systems tax every business corporation at entity level under Part I of the federal Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act. Statutory elections relevant to this software exporter include: (i) GST/HST section 156 election to deem taxable supplies between a parent and a closely related corporation (90-percent or greater control) to be at nil consideration; (ii) GST/HST Quick Method election for smaller registrants; (iii) GST/HST annual filing and net-tax threshold elections; (iv) corporate income tax capital dividend election under subsection 83(2) and paid-up capital election under subsection 89(5); (v) for hybrid mismatch arrangements, no elective relief exists and the BEPS Action 2 rule set is implemented mechanically through Income Tax Act sections 18.2 to 18.23 and section 20.2, which deny deductions for hybrid leakage regardless of taxpayer designation. Revenu Quebec harmonizes QST elections with CRA under the intergovernmental single-administration agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_optional_n: Not applicable - Canada is not a check-the-box jurisdiction and no hybrid mismatch election is available; hybrid mismatch rules apply compulsorily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT system in Quebec: federal GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) at 5 percent plus provincial QST (Quebec Sales Tax) at 9.975 percent administered by Revenu Quebec; Quebec is not a harmonized-sales-tax province, so the federal component remains GST at 5 percent and is stacked with the separate QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold on annual worldwide taxable supplies; QST: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold on annual worldwide taxable supplies; a non-resident supplier of digital gaming services to Canadian consumers must register under the simplified GST/QST electronic regime once its taxable supplies to Canadian recipients exceed the same CAD 30,000 threshold; registration is voluntary below the threshold and zero-rated export supplies do not trigger compulsory registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently maintain a live fiscal-clearance or digital-stamping mandate for GST/HST or QST invoices; the CRA and Revenu Quebec accept paper, PDF, EDI, or XML invoice records meeting the prescribed content rules (supplier legal name, business number, date, description, tax rate, tax amount, recipient identifiers). Revenu Quebec is transitioning toward mandatory B2B electronic invoicing on the PEPPOL network, with phased obligations projected from September 2027 for large taxpayers (annual turnover above CAD 50 million) and later phases expected to cover SMEs and digital service exporters. No QR-code invoice, API clearance, or real-time pre-approval of invoices is required anywhere in the Canadian GST/QST system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies where the anti-cheat middleware software is supplied to a foreign-located game publisher or cloud infrastructure: (a) intangible personal property supplied to a non-resident and not for use in Canada qualifies under Schedule VI, Part II, section 22 of the Excise Tax Act; (b) services supplied to a non-resident, including cloud-hosted middleware APIs, fall under Schedule VI, Part V, section 23 when the service is not rendered to an individual present in Canada and does not relate to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada; (c) physically exported goods such as development kits, hardware authentication modules, or server appliances qualify under Schedule VI, Part I. The Canadian supplier must document the recipient's non-residency, the foreign place of supply, and the foreign consumption/benefit of the software. For Quebec QST, the same export zero-rating exists under the Quebec Sales Tax Act, and the exporter is entitled to QST input tax refunds plus federal GST input tax credits for expenses attributable to the zero-rated export sales.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration filed through the Canadian International Trade Single Window or equivalent customs export entry for shipped physical goods, including gaming hardware, server appliances, and development kits
Customs bill of lading (ocean, air, or truck) or freight waybill showing the Canadian point of shipment and the foreign destination port
Commercial invoice and signed anti-cheat middleware software license or subscription agreement identifying the foreign gaming publisher, license scope, and end-user location
Airway bill or courier receipt for physical shipments of prototype devices or instrumented hardware leaving Canada

Digital delivery logs from CDN/cloud platforms, cryptographic hash receipts, or server transfer records proving the software SDK, updates, and telemetry services were transmitted to servers outside Canada
SWIFT MT103 wire transfer receipt and bank statement evidencing inward remittance from the foreign buyer into the Canadian corporation's bank account within normal commercial credit terms
Non-resident buyer status evidence such as a foreign incorporation certificate, foreign VAT/GST registration number, or statutory declaration of non-residency
Server geolocation logs and IP address records demonstrating that the gaming anti-cheat engine was installed, monitored, or accessed from outside Canada
Export transaction worksheets and inter-company pricing documentation where the sale is made to a related foreign entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess disallowed zero-rated export supplies retroactively within four years in the normal audit cycle, extended to eight years where misrepresentation is shown and unlimited where fraud is established. A clawback recovers the full combined 14.975 percent exposure (5 percent GST plus 9.975 percent QST) plus prescribed daily compounded interest from the original reporting deadline. Civil penalties apply under Excise Tax Act section 280 at 25 percent of net tax for false statements and section 285 at 50 percent for gross negligence, with equivalent QST penalties under Quebec's Tax Administration Act. Criminal prosecution under Excise Tax Act section 327 or Quebec tax offence provisions may lead to fines of up to 200 percent of the evaded tax and terms of imprisonment. The exporter must retain all customs, banking, and digital delivery records for six years, and bears the burden of proving the foreign destination, the buyer's non-resident status, and the actual export of the software or service.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — sovereign monetary and currency authority; the Minister of Finance (Department of Finance Canada) holds formal foreign-exchange policy powers under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act; OSFI supervises authorized financial institutions; FINTRAC administers cross-border wire and AML reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); Revenu Québec administers provincial tax and registration matters. Canada maintains no exchange-control board, licensing, or permit authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account. There are no exchange-control approvals, no quotas, no surrender obligations, and no central-bank authorization to file for equity injections, dividends, royalties, shareholder-loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds. The only structural frictions are (i) FINTRAC reporting by the financial institution of any cross-border electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more; (ii) Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) withholding on non-resident payments — dividends 25% (treaty-reduced to 5% for a US parent owning 10%+), royalties 25% (treaty-reduced to 0–10%), interest 25% on non-arm's-length shareholder loans (treaty-reduced, e.g., 0% under the Canada-US treaty for qualifying arm's-length interest), and arm's-length portfolio interest exempt under domestic law; and (iii) the Investment Canada Act notification for a non-Canadian establishing a new Canadian business with aggregate gross assets exceeding CAD 5M. No Quebec-specific convertibility restriction applies to a software-licensing exporter.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada does not impose a repatriation timeline, a mandatory conversion ratio, or a holding limitation on export proceeds. The anti-cheat engine's licensing and maintenance revenues invoiced in USD, EUR, CNY, or KRW may be retained indefinitely in foreign-currency bank accounts in Canada or abroad, converted at the company's election, or used directly for outbound trade settlement. The binding obligations are limited to (i) FINTRAC reporting of any cross-border electronic transfer at or above CAD 10,000 in or out of Canada; (ii) the corporate bank's own monitoring of conversion patterns against the declared treasury policy; and (iii) transfer-pricing documentation requiring that the Quebec entity bill non-resident affiliates at arm's-length rates for its software and services.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Operating Account (CAD) + US Dollar Business Account at the Montreal head office; optional 'Capital Call Sub-Account' for segregated equity injection (no statutory capital escrow is imposed on a Quebec QBCA corporation).
Canadian Dollar Business Operating Account + USD Advantage Account (eligible for inbound USD licensing receipts); capital contribution received into a segregated Business Sub-Account.
Canadian Dollar Business Chequing Account + USD Business Account with borderless USD clearing; full SWIFT MT103 origination at the Toronto main branch.
Business Performance Plan (CAD) + USD Business Account; capital injections may be routed into a separate Everyday Business Account before transfer to operating funds.
Business Operating Account (CAD) + Scotiabank USD Account; international trade-services desk available in Montreal.
Business Operating Account (CAD) + USD Business Account; eligibility for CIBC Global FX desk forward and swap documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a collection gateway (Stripe, Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer), but Medium-Low as the primary treasury concentration point. Foreign EMIs are not Canadian Schedule I banks, are not CDIC-insured, and provide payment services in Canada as FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (MSBs). Legally, the Quebec entity may use an EMI to collect low-value B2B licensing fees, but the EMI should be limited to a pre-funded acquisition rail with a daily automated sweep to the primary Schedule I bank account. Holding the full treasury balance at an offshore EMI creates (i) unregistered deposit-taking risk under provincial law, (ii) FINTRAC and sanctions compliance gaps, (iii) no access to Payments Canada Lynx RTGS settlement, and (iv) no eligibility for FX forwards or a derivatives master agreement. Policy rule: any invoice exceeding CAD 10,000 should be paid by SWIFT MT103 directly to the Canadian bank so that FINTRAC reporting remains with the licensed institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal or Quebec statute requires an in-person bank visit for corporate account opening, but bank-level KYC practice effectively requires it in two scenarios: (a) when the sole signing director is a non-resident with no Canadian address, and (b) when the account will be granted FX dealing limits. The tier-1 banks permit fully remote video onboarding where signing officers hold Canadian identity documents and the registered office is verified through the Quebec Registraire des entreprises. For a wholly-owned foreign parent, banks commonly require the foreign director to attend one in-branch interview in Montreal or Toronto, or the appointment of a Quebec-resident officer as account signatory. Recommended action: appoint a Montreal-based director or delegate signing authority to the entity's Canadian controller; complete the initial interview in-branch at National Bank or RBC; then conduct all subsequent onboarding and signing-authority changes by video and certified true copies. Full onboarding for a Low_Risk_Standard software exporter typically finalizes within 5–10 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent with 100% ownership and no Canadian nexus triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD) and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) disclosure at the 25% threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Quebec Business Corporations Act articles and Registraire des entreprises certificate of good standing; NEQ and federal GST/HST business-number confirmations; register of directors; UBO register with passport copies; group organizational chart; source-of-funds declaration and bank referral letters from the parent's home institution; board resolution authorizing account opening and each signing officer; written confirmation that no nominee or bearer shares exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank misclassifies 'gaming anti-cheat engine' as gambling, iGaming, or money-transmission and issues a prohibited-business rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a third-party industry attestation confirming ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511; product narrative stating the software supplies kernel-level anti-cheat integrity middleware for game publishers (no betting, no real-money gaming, no stored value); executed Master License Agreements listing established studios; sample B2B invoices showing recurring software-licensing fees; counsel's responsibility letter confirming that no Canadian gaming, lottery, or money-services licence is required; financial statements or a business plan demonstrating B2B-only revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border equity injection from a low-transparency jurisdiction flagged as a potential layering transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the executed share-subscription agreement and paid-up-capital board resolution; intercompany loan agreement if debt-financed; audited or management accounts of the funding parent; bank statements evidencing funds provenance immediately before the transfer; the corporate law opinion confirming valid issuance; the shareholder register updated contemporaneously; the Canadian tax adviser's written confirmation of paid-up-capital treatment; and the completed FINTRAC cross-border wire-report acknowledgment from the receiving bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume inbound receipts from Korea, China, and Europe via SWIFT and Stripe raising an unexplained-volume alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a 12-month treasury forecast by jurisdiction; published pricing schedule and customer contracts; the reconciliation policy mapping invoice → Stripe settlement → daily sweep → SWIFT receipt; a pre-approved de minimis notification covenant with the relationship manager (e.g., pre-notification for any single receipt above CAD 500,000); and an annual attestation by the CFO confirming all software revenues derive from B2B licensing contracts with no consumer-facing money transmission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Gouvernement du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end, per the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of approximately CAD 30; administrative strike-off/dissolution may occur after two consecutive years of failure to file the annual declaration, subject to restoration procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (T2) with GIFI and applicable schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty is 5% of unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; persistent non-filing can lead to enforcement, interest accrual, and ministerial assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (Revenu Québec CO-17 equivalent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid Quebec tax, plus compounding daily interest; additional penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act for willful default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec non-distributing business corporation is exempt from a shareholder-required auditor appointment only if all shareholders consent to dispense with an auditor. Publicly distributing corporations, corporations subject to regulated-sector requirements, or corporations whose shareholders holding at least 10% of voting shares demand an audit must appoint an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the default; IFRS may be adopted voluntarily or is required for publicly accountable enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Shareholding ownership is recorded in the corporate registers with each issuance or transfer; the Quebec Annual Declaration must reflect correct director, officer, and registered office information. No separate federal UBO filing applies to a Quebec provincial corporation, but if the entity were constituted under CBCA, a Register of Individuals with Significant Control would also be required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Securities Issued and Transfers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined general corporate income tax rate: 26.5% (15.0% federal plus 11.5% Quebec). A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a 9.0% federal small-business rate on eligible active business income within the applicable business limit; Quebec rates and eligibility rules must be separately satisfied.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development regime, federal Investment Tax Credits, Quebec research and development credits, Quebec refundable multimedia title and video-game-related credits where statutory conditions are met, and the Quebec small-business rate for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations. Eligibility depends on expenditure type, ownership, activity, registration, documentation, and applicable annual limits. Tax holidays are not generally available for an ordinary Quebec software corporation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Canada Revenue Agency Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed through the CRA-approved electronic corporate filing system, generally certified by an authorized representative or corporate officer. Quebec corporations also file Revenu Quebec Form CO-17, Corporation Income Tax Return, through Revenu Quebec's electronic filing channel where electronic filing is required or used.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; corporate tax installments are generally monthly, or quarterly where statutory eligibility conditions are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return is due within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any balance is generally payable two months after year-end, or three months after year-end for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations meeting the statutory conditions. Quebec Form CO-17 is generally due within six months after the fiscal year-end. Tax installments are due under the applicable monthly or quarterly schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, corporation type, tax year, fiscal year-end, address, province of residence, incorporation jurisdiction, and principal business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned Canadian corporation reports its Canadian legal entity and Canadian fiscal period. Ownership status must be accurately disclosed; non-resident ownership does not eliminate Canadian corporate filing obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related and associated corporations, ownership, control, and association information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign parent, affiliates, common-control entities, and associated corporations where applicable. Do not characterize control solely by formal share ownership if factual control exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting income or loss to income for tax purposes, including non-deductible expenses, timing adjustments, and tax-specific inclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Canadian statutory accounts to Canadian tax results. Foreign accounting treatment, transfer-pricing adjustments, shareholder expenses, and non-arm's-length charges require separate review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, federal tax calculation, applicable credits, surtaxes, and federal income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the correct general, small-business, investment, or other applicable rate. A non-resident-owned corporation generally cannot claim Canadian-controlled private corporation benefits unless it satisfies the statutory ownership and control tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or applicable capital-cost schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of taxable income, capital cost allowance, reserves, loss utilization, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only for expenditures incurred to earn income and supported by contemporaneous records. Software development costs, acquired intellectual property, depreciable property, and internally developed assets require classification analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 31 or applicable investment-tax-credit schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal investment tax credits, including qualifying scientific research and experimental development expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document Canadian work locations, personnel, technical uncertainty, experimentation, eligible expenditures, subcontracting, and government assistance. Foreign development work generally requires separate eligibility analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder information for corporations with significant ownership thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign corporate shareholders, ownership percentages, and other required shareholder data. Maintain beneficial ownership evidence and ownership-chain records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign affiliate information and information return for non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Form T106 where the reporting threshold and statutory conditions are met. Include cross-border royalties, management fees, development services, loans, guarantees, cost-sharing, and other related-party transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 9 and Schedule 97, where applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party disclosures and information concerning non-resident entities or foreign affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile disclosures to financial statements, transfer-pricing records, withholding tax slips, customs data, and intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Quebec CO-17, Corporation Identification and Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income allocation, Quebec tax calculation, payments, refundable credits, and corporate identification data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to Quebec using the applicable allocation rules and maintain records supporting Quebec permanent establishment, payroll, revenue, assets, and business activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec research, development, multimedia, employment, and other credit claims, where available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File only credits supported by qualifying Quebec activities, approved applications, payroll evidence, project records, and required certificates. Credits may be reduced by assistance, related-party payments, or expenditure limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T4, T5, NR4, RL-1, and RL-3 information slips
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employment income, dividends, interest, royalties, and other reportable payments to residents and non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold and remit amounts before payment where required. Obtain valid treaty documentation before applying reduced non-resident withholding rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For a late T2 return with tax owing, the ordinary federal penalty is generally 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late, up to 12 months; repeat late filers may face 10% plus 2% per month, subject to statutory limits. Quebec generally applies a 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month, with enhanced repeat-failure penalties. Interest is generally compounded daily at prescribed rates. Additional penalties may apply for false statements, gross negligence, failure to file information returns, failure to remit source deductions, or failure to maintain records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA Form T106, Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents of Canada, filed electronically with the T2 return where required. CRA Form T1134 may apply for foreign affiliates. Country-by-Country Reporting Form RC4649 may apply to a qualifying multinational enterprise group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T106 is generally due by the corporation's T2 filing deadline. T1134 generally has a separate filing deadline linked to the taxpayer's tax year. RC4649 is generally due within 12 months after the fiscal year-end of the reporting fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canadian reporting entity, tax year, business activity, and identification data for each non-resident related party.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use legal names, tax residence, jurisdiction, relationship, and taxpayer identification data that reconcile to contractual and payment records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transaction category, gross amount, currency, payment or receipt direction, and relationship information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross transaction amounts rather than netting receipts and payments. Separately identify services, royalties, interest, financing, goods, guarantees, and other categories.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing methodology, arm's-length pricing, and documentation information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the selected method agrees with the contemporaneous documentation, functional analysis, tested party, comparables, and actual invoicing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Country-by-country revenue, profit, taxes, employees, tangible assets, and constituent-entity data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File only where the group satisfies the Canadian reporting conditions, including the applicable consolidated revenue threshold and reporting-entity rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T106 may attract a penalty generally based on the number of days late, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Gross negligence, repeated non-compliance, incomplete information, or failure to provide transfer-pricing records may trigger additional penalties, reassessment, and extended audit periods.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The Canadian domestic Part XIII withholding tax rate on dividends paid or credited to a non-resident is generally 25%. A treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders meeting ownership conditions and 15% for other portfolio shareholders under many treaties. The Canada-United States treaty commonly provides 5% for qualifying corporate ownership and 15% otherwise, subject to limitation-on-benefits and other conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer must obtain sufficient evidence of the recipient's identity, beneficial ownership, tax residence, and treaty entitlement before applying a reduced rate. CRA Form NR301 is commonly used for corporate beneficial-owner certification; NR302 and NR303 address certain partnership and hybrid arrangements. A valid certificate of residence or equivalent tax-residence evidence may be required under the relevant treaty and CRA administrative practice. The payer must remit withholding to the CRA by the statutory remittance deadline, file Form T4A-NR or NR4 as applicable, and retain documentation. Treaty relief is not automatic and may be denied under beneficial-ownership, anti-conduit, limitation-on-benefits, principal-purpose, or similar anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% for royalties and certain interest payments to non-residents. Arm's-length interest that is not participating interest is generally exempt from Canadian withholding under domestic law, subject to statutory exceptions; related-party interest and other specified interest may remain subject to withholding. Treaty rates vary. Many Canadian treaties limit royalties to approximately 10% and interest to approximately 10%, while some treaties provide lower rates or exemptions for qualifying government, financial, or arm's-length interest. Software, database, cloud, and anti-cheat technology payments require characterization analysis to distinguish royalties, services, subscriptions, and business profits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not impose a general monetary threshold before contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is required. The arm's-length requirement applies to cross-border non-arm's-length transactions. Form T106 reporting generally becomes relevant where aggregate transactions with a non-resident related party exceed CAD 1,000,000, subject to statutory exclusions and detailed rules. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational enterprise groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750 million in the preceding fiscal year. Canada has not adopted an OECD-style mandatory Master File and Local File regime using those exact labels; Canadian contemporaneous documentation fulfills the principal local documentation requirement.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a standalone general Economic Substance Regulation regime equivalent to certain offshore ESR statutes. Canadian tax authorities apply the arm's-length principle, transfer-pricing rules, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, treaty anti-abuse provisions, beneficial-ownership principles, sham and substance-over-form doctrines, and specific anti-avoidance provisions. A Canadian corporation should maintain real decision-making, personnel, expenditure, technical capability, contractual authority, risk control, intellectual-property functions, and records consistent with its claimed profit allocation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly concealing revenue, fabricating expenses, misrepresenting Canadian activities, using false invoices, or submitting a materially false corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act, criminal conviction may result in a fine generally ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, together with imprisonment for up to two years. Civil reassessment, interest, gross-negligence penalties, and prosecution may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who personally participate in fraudulent conduct may face criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, civil recovery, and asset-restraint measures. Ordinary corporate status does not shield personal wrongdoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making a false statement or omission attributable to gross negligence, including unsupported deductions, fabricated development costs, or knowingly incorrect credit claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The federal gross-negligence penalty is generally 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed credit, in addition to tax, interest, reassessment, and possible limitation-period extension.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise for directors or officers who direct, authorize, or participate in the conduct. The corporation remains liable for the assessment and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, financing costs, or development-service prices without functional support, or shifting Canadian gaming-engine profits to a low-substance foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may adjust income under the Income Tax Act, deny or recharacterize deductions, impose transfer-pricing penalties generally equal to 10% of the adjustment where statutory conditions are met, charge interest, and apply anti-avoidance rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil exposure for breach of fiduciary or statutory duties and may be personally liable where they participated in fraud or knowingly authorized unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or other Part XIII amounts to non-residents without withholding, remitting, reporting, or retaining treaty-support documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for the unremitted withholding tax, interest, and penalties. Failure-to-deduct penalties may apply, and repeated or deliberate failures may result in prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable under the Income Tax Act for unremitted source deductions, subject to the statutory due-diligence defence. Personal assets may be pursued after corporate default.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Remit Payroll and Employment Source Deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to deduct or remit income tax, Canada Pension Plan contributions, or Employment Insurance premiums for employees or misclassifying employees as contractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessments, penalties, interest, payroll reassessments, and prosecution may apply. CRA may issue director-liability assessments for unremitted source deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unremitted amounts where the corporation failed to remit and the statutory due-diligence defence is unavailable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register, collect, report, or remit GST/HST or Quebec sales tax on taxable software, platform, subscription, or digital services, including incorrect place-of-supply treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax, interest, late-filing penalties, failure-to-remit penalties, denial of input tax credits, and audit reassessment may apply. Quebec may impose separate QST assessments and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face statutory liability for certain unremitted amounts, particularly where trust-like sales-tax or source-deduction obligations are involved, subject to applicable due diligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal Canadian company with no meaningful personnel, decision-making, technical capability, or commercial risk to obtain treaty benefits or shift anti-cheat-engine profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Benefits may be denied under beneficial-ownership rules, treaty anti-abuse provisions, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, or principal-purpose tests. Reassessments, withholding tax, interest, penalties, and reporting audits may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil and criminal exposure where the structure involves fraud, false records, deliberate evasion, or breach of corporate and fiduciary duties. A shell-company label alone is not an independent Canadian criminal offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Records and Beneficial Ownership Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining inaccurate registers, concealing controlling persons, failing to maintain corporate records, or providing false information to banks, regulators, tax authorities, or payment processors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate-law penalties, regulatory orders, tax-information penalties, account restrictions, and prosecution may apply depending on the statute and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face fines, disqualification, civil claims, and criminal liability for knowingly false filings or obstruction. Travel restrictions are not an automatic corporate penalty but may arise from criminal process or court orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing criminal proceeds, structuring transactions to avoid reporting, concealing beneficial ownership, submitting false information, or using payment rails for unlawful gaming activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act may impose administrative monetary penalties and criminal penalties, including substantial fines and imprisonment. FINTRAC obligations apply only where the entity is a reporting entity or conducts regulated activities; ordinary software development is not automatically a reporting-entity business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who participate in laundering, terrorist financing, obstruction, or reporting evasion may face prosecution, imprisonment, fines, forfeiture, asset restraint, and prohibition orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Research and Development or Multimedia Credit Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming tax credits for routine coding, non-qualifying production, foreign work, shareholder activity, duplicate costs, unsupported subcontracting, or expenditures already subsidized by another program.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Credits may be denied or recovered with interest and penalties. False or grossly negligent claims may attract a 50% penalty and, in fraudulent cases, criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly certify false technical or financial information may face personal civil and criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Electronic Records, Privacy, and Cybersecurity Misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unauthorized access to game clients or servers, deployment of anti-cheat code without authorization, exfiltration of personal data, or falsification or destruction of tax and accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code, privacy, Quebec privacy, contractual, and regulatory sanctions may apply, including fines, damages, injunctions, breach-notification obligations, and imprisonment for serious offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may be personally liable for intentional unauthorized access, fraud, data misuse, obstruction, or knowing participation. Corporate indemnification does not protect criminal conduct.
